findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There is observed to not be a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present in the facility during today’s inspection. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was observed to be ice that had been dumped in the handwashing sink at the bar. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that handwashing sinks are only used for their intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: There was observed to be a phone charging on the top of the preparation cooler on the cook-line. There was also observed to be personal canned drinks in the double-door cooler in between trays of food for the facility. Discussed making sure to store personal items in a designated area to prevent contamination to food-contact surfaces and food for the facility. It is recommended to have a bucket on the bottom shelf of a cooler labeled “Personal” for employee food and drinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The ice scoop in the bar ice basin was observed to have the handle in contact with the ice. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC, who then corrected the scoop handle to be above the ice. Employees use their bare hands to scoop ice using the ice scoop, therefore, the ice scoop should be stored with the handle above the ice to protect the ice from contamination from bare hand contact.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT- There were raw, shelled eggs on the top shelf in the walk-in cooler observed to be stored above cut onions and other cut vegetables. CORRECTED- The raw, shelled eggs were moved to the bottom shelf under ready-to-eat foods. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There are Parmesan cheese shakers observed to be stored on tables for consumer use. According to the PIC in the kitchen, these shakers are put in the cooler every night and then placed on the tables every day for consumer use. The cheese is imported grated pecorino Romano cheese from Casale and the box is stored in the walk-in cooler and states to “KEEP REFRIGERATED”. The facility can either cease this practice and store the Parmesan cheese shakers in a cooler and remove them only when a consumer wants to use them OR can reach out to the manufacturer to determine if the Parmesan cheese only needs to be refrigerated for QUALITY and not SAFETY. A follow up is scheduled for 8/5/2026 to allow time for the facility to decide and to reach out to the manufacturer. Ensure that proof is provided if reaching out to the manufacturer. If there are any questions, please reach out to the inspector.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The following food-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The ice baffle and the top of the inside of the ice machine were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- The ice baffle and the top of the inside of the ice machine were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that the ice machine is being cleaned as often as necessary to maintain it clean.

CORRECTED- The pizza cutter was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are being stored in a manner that protects them from contamination. 

Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was marinara sauce in a hot holding unit that was probed to be at 122F and 118F. An employee stated that they had recently transferred the sauce from the stove into the steam table. CORRECTED- The marinara sauce was reheated on the stove and this was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that hot holding temperatures are being monitored by employees to make sure that hot holding equipment is properly functioning. Ensure that TCS food is being hot held at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: There were reduced oxygen packaged (ROP) halibut and salmon that were observed to still be in their package and thawed in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The ROP salmon and halibut had slits cut in their packages and an employee was educated on this. Ensure that ROP fish is removed from its packaging prior to being thawed under refrigeration or is removed from its packaging immediately after being thawed.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

Ensure that sanitizer buckets are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting properly sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Two containers of meat sauces stored in the warmer were probed at 118F and 104F. The PIC mentioned  that the sauces were placed in the warmer an hour and a half prior to the inspection. The facility was instructed to reheat the meat sauces (on stovetop) to the proper reheating temperature (at least 165F). Be sure that TCS food items are always held at 135F to ensure proper hot holding temperatures.

The containers of food were removed from the floor and put on shelves. Ensure that food items are never stored on the floor and are always stored at least 6 inches above the floor.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the fans in the walk-in cooler have an accumulation of dust. Ensure fans are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust and other soil residues. The fans must be cleaned by the next routine inspection.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed caulking at the hand washing sink adjacent to the dish washing area is in disrepair leaving a large gap between the hand sink and the wall. The caulking at the triple sink in the dish washing area is also starting to deteriorate. The caulking must be repaired to make a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. Ensure that caulking is repaired by the next routine inspection. 

6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There wasn’t a CFPM at the start of the inspection. A CFPM arrived shortly afterwards. Ensure that a CFPM is present at all times to cover all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee not using a barrier when turning off faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed with PIC proper techniques. Ensure that a barrier is used to turn off faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine to have a final rinse concentration of 0ppm (CL). PIC contacted a technician to service the machine. The sanitizing tube was worn down and was replaced during the inspection. Ensure that the dish machine’s final rinse concentration is maintained at 100ppm to properly sanitize dishes. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
The drinking straws in the bar area were observed to be unwrapped and in close proximity to the customer. Discussed with PIC and straws were placed behind the counter. Ensure that drinking straws are stored in a manner that prevents them from contamination. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed cans of energy drinks to be stored with food intended for public consumption. Discussed with PIC and cans were removed. Ensure that personal items are stored separate from food and drinks that are going to be used for the public. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.
